Hopper

A puzzle for Android, seen from inside a drop of quicksilver. The drop never stops bouncing; all you choose is where the next bounce goes.

tap the black

This is a level of the game itself: its islands, grown by the game's code, and its liquid, lit by the game's own shaders. Tap to raise it again; drag to walk round it.

Download for Android Source

In the level

  • Shards glow in the pits of the islands. Take them all and the gate opens.
  • Glass holds while you bounce on it, and sinks the moment you leave.
  • Springs throw you two cells along their glowing arrow, and a floor up. They are the only way up.
  • Floors float one over another. Under a floor you can hop, but not leap: the floor is a ceiling.
  • Hot plates burn, unless you carry a silver bead to cool one.
  • Mirages look like islands and hold nothing. Over each stands a shimmering mirror, always turned to you, and in it your own drop bounces as through hot air. Near a mirage, the island ahead answers every landing with a soft note. A mirage keeps silent.
  • Rivals: from the thirty-sixth level on, a lilac drop may race you to the gate, with the same task as yours. It plays about as well as a person: it hesitates, steps aside, slips into the liquid and drops in again at the start. First through the gate wins.
  • Some levels shift. After a number of bounces the ground trembles, then everything but the island under you goes down into the liquid and a new act rises around you. Shards you did not reach move on with you.

Ten levels are drawn by hand; after them, every level is grown from its own number and checked by a solver, so there is always a next one.

The world

Every level won for the first time grows a piece of a world out of the black, in the dark before the next level. First a single crystal; then more, out of each other; then glades, branches and trees, cubes, houses with their windows lit, whole streets, towers. Now and then, without warning, something precious: a burning gem, a funnel of light, a prism. Tap the black to send the world under and wake the level.

tap to win a level

The game's own world, grown by its code: tap, and the next piece comes up out of the black.

The black drop

The hundredth level has no shards and no gate. A black drop falls in far away and comes for you by the same rules you hop by. If it lands on your island it strikes, and a slash cuts the world in two: the half without you tips over the edge and goes into the black, and what is left shows its sawn islands, every step in section. A second strike, and you are lost. The only way through is down onto it from a floor above. Right under you it stops and looks up, as if working out the way: that is the moment. Beat it, and the world you grew turns to gold in a rose dawn. The game is won, and the levels go on; between the map and the eye stands a little hopscotch that opens every level and every world.

The watcher and the hopscotch

Beside the map sits the watcher, an eye in a stepped frame of bismuth. Tap it, and it plays the level for you, turning and hopping as a finger would; swipe, and the drop is yours again. After its game comes the hopscotch: every level as a chalked square, numbers climbing up the screen without end. Any level played can be played again.

Controls

  • Swipe up: the next bounce goes one cell ahead. A long swipe leaps over a cell.
  • Swipe up and aside: one cell across a corner.
  • Swipe sideways to turn, down to turn round. Tap to look at the map.
  • Tap the eye to let the watcher play. Back opens the hopscotch.
Android 8.0 or newer with OpenGL ES 3.0. Everything seen and heard is made by the code. 0BSD.
